validated_results.title: Folic acid and risk of prostate cancer: results from a randomized clinical trial.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
validated_results.reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of folic acid supplementation in men reporting incident prostate cancer diagnoses with an age-adjusted hazard ratio, confidence interval, and p value.

extraction.timing: Participants followed up to 10.8 years (median 7.0 years)
extraction.population: Men randomly assigned to placebo or folic acid supplementation in the Aspirin/Folate Polyp Prevention Study

sample_size.excerpt: Among the 643 men who were randomly assigned to placebo or supplementation with folic acid, the estimated probability of being diagnosed with prostate cancer over a 10-year period was 9.7% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 6.5% to 14.5%) in the folic acid group and 3.3% (95% CI = 1.7% to 6.4%) in the placebo group (age-adjusted hazard ratio = 2.63, 95% CI = 1.23 to 5.65, Wald test P = .01).

effect_size.excerpt: Among the 643 men who were randomly assigned to placebo or supplementation with folic acid, the estimated probability of being diagnosed with prostate cancer over a 10-year period was 9.7% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 6.5% to 14.5%) in the folic acid group and 3.3% (95% CI = 1.7% to 6.4%) in the placebo group (age-adjusted hazard ratio = 2.63, 95% CI = 1.23 to 5.65, Wald test P = .01). In contrast, baseline dietary folate intake and plasma folate in nonmultivitamin users were inversely associated with risk of prostate cancer, although these associations did not attain statistical significance in adjusted analyses.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Among the 643 men who were randomly assigned to placebo or supplementation with folic acid, the estimated probability of being diagnosed with prostate cancer over a 10-year period was 9.7% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 6.5% to 14.5%) in the folic acid group and 3.3% (95% CI = 1.7% to 6.4%) in the placebo group (age-adjusted hazard ratio = 2.63, 95% CI = 1.23 to 5.65, Wald test P = .01).

design.excerpt: a placebo-controlled randomized trial of aspirin and folic acid supplementation

timing.excerpt: Participants were followed for up to 10.8 (median = 7.0, interquartile range = 6.0-7.8) years
